title: Choosing tiles for a bathroom: what to look for
excerpt: A bathroom is where humidity, temperature changes and daily use come together. Practical advice on choosing surface, format and colour.
body:
In a bathroom, tiles must be safe and practical as well as beautiful. The first rule is to choose different surfaces for floor and walls. On the floor, a matt or slightly textured surface reduces slipping, while on the wall a polished finish adds light.

The format depends on the size of the room. In small bathrooms, 300×600 wall tiles and 600×600 floor tiles look well balanced. In larger rooms, the 600×1200 format reduces the number of joints and makes the surface seamless.

As for colour, light tones expand the space, dark tones bring depth and calm. Marble-look ROMA collections suit classic schemes, while concrete- or terrazzo-look ITALICA collections fit a modern interior.

Pay attention to the joint colour. Grout close to the tile colour makes the surface read as one, while contrasting grout emphasises the geometry. Choose a moisture-resistant grout for wet rooms.

Before the final decision, look at samples under the lighting of your own bathroom. Samples can be borrowed from our showroom, the most reliable way to avoid mistakes.
